    <abstract>In this paper, we developed a model explaining how social and infrastructural factors empower women entrepreneurs to achieve economic autonomy. The study employed a two-faceted method of analysis through the application of Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to test hypotheses and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) to validate the predictions. The mediation analysis revealed that social capital mediates the relationships between market linkage, sociocultural interventions, and access to finance, highlighting its vital mediating role. Cronbach’s alpha values of 0.793−0.814 and the AVE values of more than 0.70 were used to ensure reliability and validity. In the case of ANN analysis, predictive accuracy, and model generalization were useful in validating the analysis, with R values of 0.842 to 0.862 in training, 0.789 to 0.794 in validation, and 0.831 to 0.840 in testing, and Mean Squared Error values of between 0.43 and 0.70 were used to confirm stabilized learning. The paper concludes that establishing trust-based community networks, market networks, and sociocultural support systems could be very important in augmenting financial autonomy and sustainable empowerment in rural women. It is based on the Social Capital Theory and it examines the role played by sociocultural intervention and market linkage infrastructure in the accessibility of finance by women mediated by social capital. Collectively, these results indicate that although PLS-SEM provides important linear causal associations, ANN supplements the former, because it can represent nonlinear interdependencies and enhance predictive strength.</abstract>
